anchors: which does steps 2 to 5 with the CT frozen
A program's own multi-step update is not made whole
Never split the script into separate calls
Two routes run no overlay snapshot code at all; offer them before
A rootfs-only snapshot misses every `mpN` volume
Save the CT config, which no ZFS snapshot holds
decision: On a build the guard refuses, offer a raw zfs snapshot of EVERY managed volume of a CT whose managed volumes are all on zfspool storage, plus a copy of the CT config, before BINDSNAP-UNSUPPORTED: by hand for a STOPPED CT, and for a RUNNING CT as one script on the node that maps volumes via pct config, pvesm path and zfs list, copies the config, arms a trap running lxc-unfreeze, runs lxc-freeze and takes ONE zfs snapshot. State it as crash-consistent (whole system calls, not a program's multi-step update). A managed volume on non-ZFS storage still goes to vzdump.

evidence.text: The script was run on a nested test node with pve-container 6.1.24 (rootfs plus one volume mp1, a writer running): CT FROZEN during the snapshot and RUNNING after, both volumes in one zfs snapshot with equal counters for a write-then-rename writer, a truncate-then-write file caught EMPTY, writer continued after thaw, pct listsnapshot does not list it, a duplicate name created nothing and the trap still thawed, stop plus zfs rollback per volume plus start restored the state. Stock behaviour read in pve-container 6.1.24 Config.pm (__snapshot_freeze) and PVE::Storage::Plugin volume_snapshot_needs_fsfreeze. RED (opus, pre-edit text) found no route that keeps the CT running and is instant; GREEN (opus, haiku) ran the script route and sent an lvmthin rootfs to vzdump.

reopen_if: A run shows lxc-freeze leaving a CT frozen after the script exits, or stock pct snapshot of a running CT on ZFS starts doing more than freeze, per-volume snapshot and thaw (for example an fsfreeze), or Proxmox's ZFS plugin stops refusing a rollback past a newer snapshot.
why: Amends the stopped-only rule on a user decision 2026-11-19 ("Add freeze route (Recommended)"): the old rule sent every running CT to vzdump, a slow full copy, so a running CT that must not stop had no quick sanctioned path. Stock pct snapshot of a running CT does the same freeze, per-volume snapshot and thaw, and adds no filesystem freeze for ZFS, so the route is the stock procedure minus the overlay's gate. This answers the old entry's reopen_if only in part; what changed is the user's ruling plus a node run of the procedure.

anchors: The gate covers creating a snapshot only
decision: Say that the untested-build gate covers creating a snapshot only: pct delsnapshot (CT running or stopped) and pct rollback of a snapshot that already exists run on any build.

evidence.text: lib/PVE/LXC/BindSnap.pm: the snapshot_delete and snapshot_rollback wrappers log a summary and call the upstream method with no checksum or running check (only snapshot_create holds the gates); a pct delsnapshot of a running CT on an untested pve-container 6.1.20 build went through on 2026-11-17.

reopen_if: The overlay starts gating snapshot_delete or snapshot_rollback on the checksum.
why: A reader who sees the gate refuse a create concludes the overlay blocks all snapshot work and does not try to clean up old snapshots natively.

decision: Rejected: a raw zfs snapshot of a RUNNING CT without lxc-freeze around it.

evidence.text: User decision 2026-11-19, option "Raw snapshot, no freeze" not chosen; "Add freeze route (Recommended)" chosen.

reopen_if: lxc-freeze proves unreliable on nodes (stalls or failed thaws in practice) where an unfrozen atomic snapshot would have done.

anchors: a backup taken as a safety net for a data volume (a database on `mp1`) silently holds none of that data
decision: Before a vzdump safety net, check every managed mpN line in pct config for backup=1 (off unless set), set it by repeating the current value plus backup=1, and confirm from the task log's including/excluding lines that each needed volume is in the archive.

evidence.text: pve-container 6.1.24 source: PVE/LXC/Config.pm mountpoint_backup_enabled (reason disabled when backup is unset), VZDump/LXC.pm include/exclude loginfo lines, __mountpoint_config_fast_plug_safe lists backup and replicate as live-changeable. RED opus and haiku on the earlier text, GREEN and quote-back opus and haiku on the new text.

reopen_if: Stock pve-container changes mountpoint_backup_enabled so that a volume mount point is backed up by default.
why: Stock vzdump includes a volume mount point only when backup is set, so an archive taken as the safety net for a data volume silently holds none of its data. A RED probe given the earlier text had to supply the check from its own Proxmox knowledge and named the trap as a skill gap.

anchors: The restore leaves the CT stopped; `pct start <vmid>`
decision: Give the concrete route back to a vzdump archive over the same CT: pct stop, then pct restore <vmid> <archive> --force 1 with the volume ID from pvesm list, and pct start afterwards because the restore leaves the CT stopped.

evidence.text: pve-container 6.1.24 PVE/API2/LXC.pm create_vm: force (Allow to overwrite existing container), start default 0, die can't overwrite running container. Quote-back opus and haiku answered from the new sentences verbatim.

reopen_if: pct restore starts the CT by default or allows overwriting a running CT.
why: RED and GREEN probes both reported that the paragraph named pct restore with no syntax, so going back was not a concrete step.

anchors: Only `root@pam` can carry a bind/device mount, because Proxmox lets no other user set one
decision: A clone carries a bind/device mpN only for root@pam; any other caller's clone is refused with the 'only allowed for root@pam' message and creates nothing, unless every bind/device mount is excluded with BINDSNAP-EXCLUDE, which needs no root. Troubleshooting tells this refusal apart from the bare 'unable to clone mountpoint' of an inactive override.

evidence.text: pve-container 6.1.26 lab node, 1.9.2 vs 1.10.0: a cloner@pve API token got mp0 carried under 1.9.2 and HTTP 500 with the root@pam message under 1.10.0; with BINDSNAP-EXCLUDE: mp0 the same token's clone succeeded without mp0; pct clone as root@pam carried mp0 on both. RED opus and haiku on the earlier text, GREEN and quote-back opus and haiku on the new text.

reopen_if: Stock check_ct_modify_config_perm lets a user other than root@pam set a bind/device mount point.
why: Up to 1.9.2 the clone override carried bind mounts for any user holding VM.Clone, which granted a host path that stock Proxmox lets only root@pam set (PR #2). The RED probes on the earlier text both called the new refusal an inactive override or guessed the rule from general Proxmox knowledge.

anchors: A CT whose **rootfs** is a bind/device mount (`rootfs: /some/host/dir`) is never cloned
decision: A CT whose rootfs is a bind/device mount is never cloned, by any user and on any build: it fails with Proxmox's own 'unable to clone mountpoint rootfs (type bind)', creates nothing, and pve-bindsnap has no route around it.

evidence.text: pve-container 6.1.26 lab node: under 1.9.2 pct clone of a CT whose rootfs is a host directory created a clone whose rootfs was the same directory; under 1.10.0 it exited 2 with unable to clone mountpoint 'rootfs' (type bind) and created no CT.

reopen_if: pve-bindsnap gains a supported route to copy a host-directory rootfs.
why: Up to 1.9.2 a root@pam clone of such a CT got the same host directory as its rootfs, so two containers shared one root filesystem. The RED probes read the rootfs refusal as an inactive override and planned a reinstall or a vetting request.

anchors: A `--snapname` clone reads the directive frozen into THAT snapshot, not the current Notes
decision: A --snapname clone reads the BINDSNAP-EXCLUDE directive frozen into that snapshot, not the current Notes: the line must be in the Notes before the snapshot is taken, or in the description given when taking it, never added to an existing snapshot's description. A managed mpN that snapshot excluded is left out of the clone with a TASK WARNINGS.

evidence.text: Unit tests t/18-snapname-left-out.t run each shipped clone_vm variant's own loop: before the fix all six queued the excluded mp1 for a --snapname clone, after it none does while a live clone and a plain-CT snapshot still clone mp1. Quote-back on opus and haiku answered the stale-snapshot question from the new sentence.

reopen_if: pve-bindsnap starts reading the live Notes for a --snapname clone.
why: The docs and skill told readers only to add the directive to the source Notes, which a --snapname clone of an older snapshot ignores; and the 1.10.0 overlay queued an excluded managed volume for clone-from-snapshot although it has no snapshot data (PR #2, sasha-id).
